name: Malawi
headline: Malawi: +2.5% growth in 2025, 28.4% inflation, debt 97% of GDP
sections: Malawi is a $15.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 147th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $1,899 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.0% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 28.4% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, up from 20.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.1% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 97% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 54% in 2020. The general government balance is −10.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −13.8% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 39% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 68% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 67.6 years (2024). Population: 24.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
